skill.name: browser-act
skill.description: Automates JavaScript-rendered browsing, extraction, interactions, screenshots, network capture, and isolated sessions through the browser-act CLI.
skill.summary: Control browser sessions and complex web workflows from supported AI agents.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: All seven static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, ordinary links, or separate screenshot and upload capabilities. However, the skill loads unaudited instructions from the installed CLI and can transmit challenge images to an external verification service.

remediation.issue: The audited file delegates its actual workflow to content returned by the installed CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Publish the complete versioned workflow in the repository and include it in every marketplace audit.

remediation.issue: Challenge images may be sent to an unspecified external verification service.
remediation.suggestion: Identify the service, document retention, crop sensitive context, and request confirmation before every transmission.

remediation.issue: The installation command retrieves an external Python package without an integrity constraint.
remediation.suggestion: Publish package provenance and provide a hash-verified installation method for the pinned version.

content.value_statement: JavaScript-heavy sites and interactive workflows are difficult to handle with basic fetch tools. browser-act provides rendered extraction, browser control, session isolation, and network capture.
actual_capabilities: Fetch and extract content rendered by JavaScript.
Navigate pages and perform clicks, typing, selections, and form actions.
Maintain isolated browser profiles and authenticated sessions.
Capture screenshots, XHR responses, fetch responses, and HAR data.
Operate multiple browser environments and URLs in parallel.
Support headed workflows, manual assistance, and user-configured proxies.
limitations: Requires Python 3.12 or newer, uv, and the browser-act CLI.
The repository file delegates detailed guidance to the installed CLI.
Browser profiles and session logs require local filesystem access.
Captcha assistance can transmit a challenge image to an external service.

use_cases.title: Extract Rendered Research
use_cases.description: Collect visible content from JavaScript-heavy pages and pages that reveal information after scrolling or interaction.

use_cases.title: Verify Web Interfaces
use_cases.description: Inspect rendered layouts, capture screenshots, and confirm interactive behavior across browser sessions.

use_cases.title: Automate Repeated Operations
use_cases.description: Run approved navigation, form, and multi-account workflows while keeping browser profiles isolated.

prompt_templates.title: Extract One Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL] and extract the main rendered text. Report the page title, key facts, and any content hidden behind interaction.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner extraction from one JavaScript-rendered page.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a User Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], follow the path from [start] to [destination], and describe each visible state. Ask before any submission or login.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an interactive website.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Isolated Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create approved isolated sessions for [accounts]. Compare the rendered results at [URL] without sharing cookies or profile data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison across separate browser identities.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Network Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce [workflow], capture relevant XHR, fetch, and HAR activity, then summarize request timing, failures, and response behavior. Exclude secrets from the report.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced diagnosis of a complex browser workflow.

output_examples.input: Extract the rendered pricing details from the requested product page.
output_examples.output: The page shows three plans: Starter, Team, and Enterprise. Team includes shared workspaces, while Enterprise requires a sales inquiry.

output_examples.input: Inspect the checkout path without submitting an order.
output: The cart opens with one item and an editable quantity.
Checkout requests contact and delivery details.
The review step appears before payment confirmation.

output_examples.input: Investigate why the dashboard stops loading after sign-in.
output_examples.output: The dashboard shell rendered, but one data request returned an authorization error. Sensitive headers were excluded from the summary.

best_practices: Request confirmation before login, submission, upload, browser creation, or deletion.
Use separate browser profiles for different accounts and trust boundaries.
Remove credentials, cookies, and personal data from screenshots and network reports.
anti_patterns: Do not submit forms, upload files, or solve challenges without explicit user approval.
Do not reuse one authenticated profile across unrelated users or accounts.
Do not load external runtime instructions that have not passed the same security review.

faq.question: What does browser-act automate?
faq.answer: It handles rendered extraction, navigation, page interaction, screenshots, network capture, and isolated browser sessions.

faq.question: Does it work with JavaScript-heavy websites?
faq.answer: Yes. It runs a browser engine and can extract content produced after JavaScript execution.

faq.question: Can it preserve authenticated sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. It stores browser profiles locally and supports isolated sessions for separate accounts.

faq.question: What requires user confirmation?
faq.answer: Installation, browser creation, login, form submission, file upload, and other sensitive operations require approval.

faq.question: Does it send data outside the machine?
faq.answer: Captcha assistance can send a challenge image to an external verification service. Other listed browser data remains local.

faq.question: Where do the detailed operating instructions come from?
faq.answer: The repository file directs the agent to load them from the installed browser-act CLI.
